newsitem.title: CROATIA: U.S. presses Croatia on lawlessness in Bosnia town.
newsitem.headline: U.S. presses Croatia on lawlessness in Bosnia town.

text.p: The United States put pressure on Croatia on Thursday to step up efforts to revive law and order in the bitterly divided southern Bosnian town of Mostar which was rocked by a shooting incident earlier this month.
U.S. Ambassador Peter Galbraith met Croatian Foreign Minister Mate Granic to underscore Zagreb's obligations to help the Bosnian peace process, the state news agency HINA reported.
The meeting took place on Galbraith's demand, hours after Western diplomats welcomed what seemed to be an organised crackdown by Croatian police on crime and Croat warlords in Mostar.

Police arrested the leader of Mostar's paramilitary mafia, Mladen Naletilic, near the Croatian city of Split on Monday. Bosnian Croat police have arrested five Croat men and issued warrants for another three on Wednesday.

Galbraith said the United States demanded full implementation of the report by International Police Task Force in Bosnia (IPTF) on the incident in which Croat police fired on a group of Moslem civilians trying to visit a cemetry in the Croat part of Mostar.
One Moslem civilian was killed and around 20 wounded.
The IPTF report named a number of Croat policemen involved in the shooting and demanded they be dismissed and prosecuted by February 26.
It also urged that Mostar's Moslem and Croat police leaders be replaced with "professional policemen from outside Mostar".

Granic said the IPTF should investigate events preceding the shooting incident. He quoted a number of Moslem "provocations", including bomb attacks on a Franciscan monastery in Mostar and a Catholic church in Sarajevo.
Galbraith said the United States would urge the Bosnian government to act in line with the report.
